subject: sample sizes, and stratification with covariates

messages.author: be2485b0836d6632
messages.subject: sample sizes, and stratification with covariates
parts:
Dear all,

I'm attempting to obtain density estimates by site and by species, for a line transect design with terrestrial birds in north Peru, as mentioned on my previous post. For some species-site combinations, the sample sizes are quite small, so, as pointed out by Eric Rexstad, one recommended way to make the most of the data is to use covariates in the distance model.

If I have two levels of stratification (species, sites), then I think there are two possibilities for analysing the data, pooling all records for a particular site (using data filter to select one site), and using species as a covariate, or pooling records for one species across all sites, and using site as a covariate (data filter to select one species). First, I'd appreciate any thoughts on whether this is a sensible way to consider the analysis, and whether one method is more appropriate than the other. Would it depend on whether I thought that species characteristics (eg vocalisations, behaviour) had more influence on detectability (therefore use site as covariate) rather than site characteristics (habitat type, structure)? Also, would there be any way of selecting a best model between the two? I don't see how I can compare AIC values from Distance if using different data filters.

I've been doing some preliminary analyses with my data, and have found that I don't always get models converging. I've tried to build up the number of covariate levels gradually, and using one key function with a low number of adjustments, (eg I'm pooling all records for a particular site, and then used species as a covariate), in this case, I added species one at a time as covariate levels with the data filter, and obtained OK looking models until hitting one or two problem species with a small number of records at that site. Are there any guidelines as to minimum sample sizes per covariate when using the multi covariate method? In some cases, there are about 10 records per site.

Of course, ideally, more records would be obtained, but for rare species, and with limited resources for field work, I think it's interesting to try to find the best methods to get decent density estimates.

I appreciate any thoughts,

best wishes,
Christian

messages.author: 1fb54f491646a589
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] sample sizes, and stratification with covariates
parts:
Christian, sorry, I didn't read your earlier posting, but on the face of it, you don't need to decide between species and site.  You can pool all data, and use both species and site as factor-type covariates.  Thus for a rare species, you use data across all sites.  But do you really need site as a factor?  Do you have covariates recorded for each site or line relating to e.g. habitat?  If so, you might model site variability in detectability by including (continuous or factor-type) covariates relating to habitat, rather than by having a level for each site of a factor.  You can post-stratify by species or site to get your abundance estimates.  In the estimate tab of model defn, you need to check both the global and stratum boxes for both density and detection function.

Steve Buckland

parts:
Many thanks for the reply.

I'd just like to clarify exactly how to get the estimates by both site and species.

In the first case you mention, where I can use both species and site as covariates,  I'm not sure how I would obtain individual density estimates by site and by species. I've tried this analysis, and I can see the detection function plots for all the site and species combinations, but the actual density estimates are either by species (if I post stratify by species) or by site (if I stratify by stratum). Is there a way of getting these detection function estimates by both sites and species (as the plots show)?

In the second case, yes, I do have habitat variables at sample level, which I can summarise to site and use this as a covariate. I'll try this as well. In this case, if, for example, I post stratify by site, does this mean that I need to do each analysis by species separately and in the case of stratifying by site, do I need to filter the data by individual sites? As in the first case, this is where I'm not sure as to how to set up the program, it would seem best to use all the data at once, but I'm not sure how to get estimates at both levels of stratification?

Thanks for the clarification and apologies for the confusion!

cheers,
Christian

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] sample sizes, and stratification with covariates
parts:
Christian:

It is possible to produce site and species-specific detection probabilities when both are covariates in the detection function.  The detection probabilities would be used to adjust counts for imperfect detectability to produce the site/species specific estimates you seek.  However Distance does not directly report those estimates for you.  Similarly Distance will only produce abundance or density estimates at levels of study area, stratum (however defined) or sample.

It would require writing some bespoke code to make the pieces fit together.  Possibly some other subscribers to the forum have suggestions.

Many thanks for the reply.

I'd just like to clarify exactly how to get the estimates by both site and species.

As in the first case, this is where I'm not sure as to how to set up the program, it would seem best to use all the data at once, but I'm not sure how to get estimates at both levels of stratification?

Thanks for the clarification and apologies for the confusion!

cheers,
Christian
